title: A first conversation between Hunter's Hope Foundation and FIN

sentences.text: At Hunter's Hope Foundation, we support families affected by Krabbe disease; Fabry International Network (FIN) supports families affected by Fabry disease.
Both conditions involve a shortage of enzymes in cells' recycling compartments and problems breaking down certain fats.
This shared biology offers a reason to explore collaboration, not proof that the same study design will suit both communities.

sections.heading: What already exists that we could share

sentences.text: Krabbe resources include The Natural History of Infantile Globoid Cell Leukodystrophy, the Krabbe Disease Global Patient Registry and KrabbeConnect's KrabbeCURES data platform.
We could explore lessons from these resources before proposing shared data collection.

sections.heading: What must be checked before we join forces

sentences.text: The enzyme shortages differ: Krabbe involves galactocerebrosidase, while Fabry involves alpha-galactosidase A.
Please help confirm whether persistent abnormal rhythmic brain-wave activity on EEG and structural differences in the medulla oblongata, part of the brainstem, also occur in Fabry disease.
We should also check reduced tissue galactocerebrosidase activity rather than assume it is a shared feature.
The atlas's predictions that certain gene-splicing changes remove protein function are inferred, unverified and below 0.5 confidence for both GALC and GLA.
Before sharing resources, let us check study eligibility and suitability for each community.

Send FIN one inquiry asking whether Natural History in Fabry Disease With IVS4+919G>A Mutations could include people with GALC-related disorders (Krabbe disease), without assuming eligibility or FIN's involvement in running it.
No open questions are recorded yet in the supplied proposal input.
I am reaching out on behalf of Hunter's Hope Foundation to explore a small collaboration.
Krabbe and Fabry disease share underlying enzyme-deficiency biology.
Could you help us ask whether Natural History in Fabry Disease With IVS4+919G>A Mutations might include Krabbe disease?
We would welcome an initial feasibility discussion, with differences and eligibility checked first.
Thank you for considering this conversation.
[Your name], on behalf of Hunter's Hope Foundation
